title: First Creole Fiesta parade and the first Mademoiselle Fiesta
summary: The fiesta had a parade from its first year, with rented fruit wagons, young girls as Mademoiselle Fiesta, and floats and carriages added as it grew.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: It's a custom, that's what it is. When did the fiesta start having parades and start having the Idol Fiesta? What year was it the first year?
It started right away? The first year.

From four people. From four people, we had a parade the very first year. And we had our first Mademoiselle Fiesta, the first year. We didn't call them queens then. We called them Mademoiselle Fiesta. That was the young girls. You know, you called them Mademoiselles. And so my granddaughter, Sylvia Serena, the daughter of the king of this year. King Edwin Serena was king this year. His daughter was the first Mademoiselle Fiesta. And we had the first parade then with five carriages. Five wagons. I had three carriages and wagons. We had those fruit. Those fruit wagons that you see those men selling? Yes. Well, we rented those. We had three of those with the children. And, oh, I have a picture. I'll look for it and show you the children who paraded in those wagons. It was all decorated with palms. I put a sheet on the wagon to cover it up and stuck palms all around. It was just beautiful. And some of the big girls now. Cynthia, who is the first, who was the maid this year to the queen, she rode in the wagon in the first parade. And wasn't that something after how many years ago? Oh, about, well, that's about seven, nine, or nine because we're ten years now. She rode in that first wagon with the little children. It was beautiful. So as the years go by, we began to expand, you see. So as it went on, we couldn't get the wagons anymore. So we had to get the, and the carriages. It was hard to get the carriages. And so we had to add these floats that we had this year. That was little children's floats. But didn't they look well? Didn't they look beautiful? Oh, yes. Well, they decorated them. And we had one for our queen, one for our king, and… Our future queens. Our future queens. Our future queens. The little girls who will be our future queens. And, of course, our carriages that the members rode in. So it's beginning to get larger all the time. And we have, we always have a convertible for our past queens. Because we want to go from the old to the new. See, we begin from the old. And the convertible, of course, is the latest. So we let the past queens ride in the convertible. With their escorts.
